title: Durable Awaiting-order cursor and queued manual ShipStation order sync

acceptanceCriteria.description: Awaiting-order progress is persisted per canonical ShipStation account and store, and a 25-page backlog with a 10-page budget advances 1-10, 11-20, then 21-25 instead of replaying page 1.
The frozen Awaiting window survives serialization/restart, rewinds safely when the provider page count shrinks, and persists new progress only after a successful pass.
Normal POST /sync/orders delegates to the existing pg-boss prepship.sync.orders job and shipstation-sync lane; it does not run syncOrders or a broad rate backfill inline.
Active, queued, retrying, and admission-error outcomes return honest backend state, while singleton admission and held-lane deadline behavior prevent competing provider execution.
PS-417 remains the backend freshness/backlog read model, and the frontend renders queued or retrying truth without declaring the sync completed.
Provider-free integration samples and two operator-triggered production requests prove the manual-sync foreground response stays below 500 ms while worker execution remains separate.
The focused and dependent sync guards, all mandatory source-of-truth guards, strict TypeScript checks, and the production frontend build pass at the reviewed SHA.

Offline verification performed no external work; the only live provider activity was the operator-approved normal Sync Orders action used for timing, which may reconcile production order data but did not buy labels/postage, send marketplace notifications, or weaken shipped/cancelled protections.

src/services/shipstation-sync-account-status.ts PS-417 per-account freshness and backlog read model

sotBypass.details: The route performs validation, queue admission delegation, and DTO mapping only. Cursor progress, queue blockers, worker execution, freshness, and targeted rate enqueueing remain in named backend owners; React does not calculate authoritative sync state.

evidence.proves: A serialized account/store cursor resumes after a simulated worker/client boundary at pages 11 and 21, reaches completion without replaying earlier pages, and remains independent of the foreground HTTP response.
A shrinking provider result rewinds by the removed page count so shifted Awaiting rows are not skipped, while growth continues from the durable cursor instead of restarting page 1.

evidence.command: npm run test:sync-job-admission && npm run test:ps-426-awaiting-cursor-manual-sync
evidence.proves: Manual incremental order refresh uses the canonical stately singleton, and an active row remains the backend blocker when active and queued candidates coexist.

evidence.command: npm run test:ps-265-job-handler-deadline && npm run test:ps-272-reaper-onpath
evidence.proves: A deliberately non-cooperative handler times out without releasing the advisory lane while its original promise is still running, and the on-path reaper does not create an overlapping successor across a held live lane.

One hundred injected-admission samples passed with p50 about 0.001 ms, p95 about 0.005 ms, and max about 0.067 ms against a 500 ms target; the harness records 100 admission calls, zero database connections, and zero provider calls. This is integration evidence, not staging/live evidence.

evidence.command: Read-only Render request/app log query for POST /sync/orders on 2026-07-16
evidence.proves: Two authenticated operator-triggered production requests returned HTTP 202 in 299 ms and 293 ms. Worker logs show both observed existing lane work, reused the already-queued busy-defer job, and left execution to one later worker claim rather than starting competing provider calls.
The normal route imports and delegates to the backend queue owner, contains no inline syncOrders or broad rate backfill, and returns the queue owner's accepted or error response.
The cursor, frozen window, backend queue ownership, frontend status pass-through, and provider-free foreground timing checks run together as the focused PS-426 command.
The existing PS-417 per-account freshness/backlog owner remains intact and PS-426 does not introduce a competing status table or resolver.

evidence.command: npm run test:ps-265-sync-run-budget && npm run test:ps-272-reaper-onpath && npm run test:ps-356-manual-order-sync-job-lane && npm run test:ps-397-order-sync-freshness && npm run test:ps-417-shipstation-sync-account-state && npm run test:sync-job-admission && npm run test:audit-sync-watchdog-lifecycle && npm run test:shipstation-sync-window
evidence.proves: The bounded-run, reaper, manual-lane, freshness, account-state, admission, watchdog, and frozen-window compatibility guards all pass.
All 45 mandatory source-of-truth and lifecycle guard commands pass with the PS-426 focused guard wired into the canonical pack.
Backend and frontend strict TypeScript checks pass.
The production frontend bundle builds successfully.

The reviewed PS-426 implementation commits change Awaiting cursor/queue orchestration and offline proof only. The only shipped-data-adjacent owner touched is order-sync.ts, where the override comments explicitly constrain the change to Awaiting query metadata. No implementation test invoked a provider or performed production mutation; the later operator-approved live timing action is recorded separately.

migrations.rollbackPlan: No database migration is involved. Revert the PS-426 implementation and timing-proof commits together; persisted JSON cursor settings are ignored by the prior application and may remain harmlessly in place.

rollback.strategy: Revert the packet/evidence commits, then revert e9b83931f94d7fc4919548faaaebcc136fd4ba80 and 95487dfa277dbbcf8e21bf8359bfa80f6fdd8a0e in that order before redeploying prepshipv4-stable. No schema rollback or production-data edit is required.

liveVerification.reason: The operator used the normal production Sync Orders toolbar control. Render recorded authenticated HTTP 202 responses in 299 ms and 293 ms, both below the 500 ms target, while worker logs independently recorded singleton/deferred execution.
